title: Set a turn-end waiting mark from the Stop hook on every turn end
action:
REWORK of a NEEDS_REVISION verdict on commit 8461cccc. Sixteen of eighteen checks passed and the full suite is green at 2050 passed. ONE defect, and it is a real one — fix exactly that, change nothing else.

THE DEFECT (judge checks K2 and P3, both FAIL). The Stop hook now reads the transcript file TWICE on every turn end:
  read #1 — mod.rs:151 calls perf_refresh(&root, session_id); that reaches html.rs:262-265, which calls resolve_transcript_for then rollup_transcript, and perf.rs:378 does read_jsonl(file).
  read #2 — mod.rs:357, inside turn_end_subject, calls read_jsonl(&path) on the same file.
reads.rs:178 read_jsonl performs an unconditional std::fs::read (reads.rs:179) with no cache between the two calls, so a large transcript is fully read and parsed twice on every single Stop.

WHY IT MATTERS. CONTEXT.md's Agent's Discretion section locks this: the resolution must be 'one resolution path, not two, and it must not add a second transcript read per turn'. The cell's own key_link K2 and prohibition P3 both restate it. The resolver reuse half is already correct — mod.rs:356 does call perf.rs:71 resolve_transcript_for. Only the second READ is wrong.

THE FIX. Thread the already-parsed events out of the perf path and feed turn_end_subject from them, instead of re-reading. Concretely: have perf_refresh (or rollup_transcript, whichever seam is cleaner in the code as it actually stands) hand back the parsed event vector — or the resolved path plus the parsed events — and pass that into the turn-end subject extraction. Read the three files yourself and pick the seam that adds the least surface; do NOT introduce a global cache, a lazy static, or a second parsing helper. After the change, exactly one std::fs::read of the transcript must happen per Stop.

PROVE IT, do not assert it. Add a test that fails on the old code and passes on the new one — count the reads rather than eyeballing the call graph. Options, pick whichever fits the existing test style: make the transcript a path whose read count is observable (a counting wrapper, or an fs fixture you can inspect), or assert on an instrumented counter you add behind cfg(test). A test that merely checks the subject is still correct does NOT prove the fix and will not be accepted — the judge's failure signature is specifically 'two full std::fs::read of the same file', so that is what your test must pin.

KEEP EVERYTHING ELSE. All seven truths, both other key_links, and all six prohibitions already PASS — do not disturb them. In particular keep: the D5 live-mark guard at mod.rs:296 and :317; the two-tier None/Some split in turn_end_subject that the judge examined and accepted (DEV-C); the Done/Crash arm placement in run_inner that the judge verified reaches every genuine Stop and no SessionEnd or PreCompact (DEV-B); and the WAITING_ON_KIND_TURN_END constant wiring (T7, K3). The perf rollup's own behaviour must not change — performance.jsonl and performance.html must still be produced exactly as before, and their existing tests must stay green.

Run the FULL suite and report its real number: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml. It gives 2050 passed, 11 ignored across 18 suites at HEAD. Note for your own sanity: a -p bee or --bins run reports 1913 and is NOT the full suite — the previous worker mistook one for the other.

truths: A Stop event with no live mark writes a waiting_on mark whose kind is turn-end and whose subject is the transcript's last non-empty assistant text line
A live gate or question mark survives a Stop untouched (per D5)
SessionEnd, PreCompact, and any non-Stop event write no mark
A missing, unreadable, or malformed transcript leaves the Stop hook's normal output intact and writes no mark
A failing store write is logged and does not fail the Stop hook
A turn whose final text block is empty or whitespace-only still produces a non-empty subject
The turn-end spelling exists exactly once in the tree, as a named constant in record.rs, and orient.rs plus the new setter both read it

artifacts.substantive: a Stop-only branch that resolves the session, reads the transcript's last text line, and calls the existing waiting-on setter behind a live-mark check
cases for the happy path, the D5 no-overwrite rule, the non-Stop events, the empty-final-text fallback, and a failure injection proving the hook survives a failing write
a pub(crate) named constant for the turn-end kind, with WAITING_ON_KIND_VALUES built from it

key_links: the setter calls the store functions in verbs/state_group/waiting_on.rs, reusing their D3 target resolution rather than resolving the target again
the transcript path comes from session_close/perf.rs's existing resolver, so the hook still reads the transcript exactly once per turn
orient.rs's blocker guard and the new setter both reference record.rs's named turn-end constant, never a literal
prohibitions: No second waiting_on writer and no second target resolver (per R128)
No provenance or source field on the mark (per D2)
No second transcript read per Stop
No text heuristic deciding whether the turn was a question (per D1)
The hook never overwrites a live mark (per D5)
No change to how a gate or question mark behaves on any surface

trace.outcome: The Stop hook writes a turn-end waiting mark on every genuine turn end, reusing the store's existing setter and D3 target resolution, never overwriting a declared gate or question mark, with the subject taken from the transcript's last non-empty assistant line. The transcript is read exactly once per Stop — one resolver, one read, proven by two read-counting tests including the late-perf-failure path that two earlier attempts leaked.

report.outcome: Stop hook sets a turn-end mark every turn end, reading the transcript exactly once
report.tests: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml — 2052 passed, 0 failed, 11 ignored, 18 suites — full declared suite, re-run independently by the judge, which also reproduced the new read-count test as red on the pre-fix code
deviations: Took two reworks: rework 1 fixed the main double read but leaked a second one whenever perf_refresh failed after its own read, and shipped a comment falsely claiming that path had no caller. Rework 2 restructured perf_refresh into PerfRefresh{events,result} so a late failure cannot discard the events, and deleted turn_end_subject fallback branch entirely rather than re-documenting an unreachable path.
Introduced WAITING_ON_KIND_TURN_END in record.rs and pointed orient.rs at it, repairing awm-1s recorded key_link miss of two drifting literals.

Marking call sits on run_inner Done and Crash arms rather than inside advisory(), so the run_stop test helper used by 18 unrelated tests gains no hidden side effect; the judge verified this reaches every genuine Stop and no SessionEnd or PreCompact.
perf.rs rollup_transcript is now test-only and carries allow(dead_code); the judge noted the stated reason for not cleaning it up was inaccurate but the outcome cosmetic.

Model independence: reworks 1 and 2 were built by different tiers, sonnet then opus, and judged by opus. The final pass is opus-built and opus-judged, so that last verdict is not model-independent; the two failures it had to survive were both found by earlier opus judges over sonnet work.

Two honest caveats, neither a rule break: the Crash arm (mod.rs:188) marks in a case an in-advisory branch would not reach, which the in-code comment at mod.rs:183-187 discloses and which favors D1; and a Stop that delegates writes no mark, a pre-existing native/Node abstention identical under either placement. The two-tier split is what the must-haves imply, not a convenient reading. T4 names a missing, unreadable, or malformed transcript and requires no mark; T6 names an empty or whitespace-only final text block and requires a non-empty subject. mod.rs:356-360 returns None only when resolve fails or read_jsonl yields zero parseable events; mod.rs:361-367 returns Some once the transcript is usable. Both tiers have their own test (tests.rs:676 and tests.rs:635). One case sits between and is unnamed by either must_have: a transcript that parses but holds no assistant entry — final_assistant_text_line returns None (mod.rs:395), unwrap_or_default makes it empty, and the fallback subject is written. That errs toward marking, which is D1's direction. Acceptable.
